summary: Both calls hold up on the reasoning I had. P1 (sell BTC/USD in full) was a pre-written stop firing: the 11-06 close of 74,756 was under the 75,317 line (10% below the 83,686 fill). It filled at 74,464.72 for about $13.05 and realized roughly a $1.60 short-term loss. The exchange-failure clause was untripped and I said so. The Skeptic's 'local bottom' objection was opinion, and I would make the same call again. I cannot tell from close.json whether BTC bounced afterward, so the sale's own test (a close back above about 80,000 within 5 sessions) is still open, and the position was too small to move the account either way. P2 (VNQ buy, resized from $20 to $12) filled at 96.81, 1.1% above the 95.73 reference, for about $11.99, and closed near 97.30 (+0.5% on cost, +1.6% on the day). I took the Skeptic's rate-sensitivity point seriously, cut the size, and sequenced the sell first. Cash is about 11.5% of equity ($71.6) against the $62.3 buffer, so the buffer held with about $9 of headroom. The account was 88.55% invested against the shadow's 99.3%. The day was a sharp rebound (VOO +2.4%, VTI +2.5%, SPY-relative return improving from -4.1% to -1.8% since 11-06), and the risk-off stance plus no new equity beta meant the account did not fully take part. One up day does not make the stance wrong, since the Market Analyst gave it only 0.45 confidence and SPY was 1% above its 200-day line. Since the version-5 start on 11-03 the agent is +1.0% against the shadow's -0.06% and SPY's -0.2%, so the cautious book has helped over the week. Account equity is $623.40 (+$7.02 on the day, drawdown 2.0%). On the held book, nothing is near a stop on the close: IDXX is about $707 against $630 (about 11% away), DPZ about $334 against $285, CARG about $34.5 against $28.25, VOO and VTI sit well above the 727.64 SPY line after a +2.4% day, and BND and IEF are still the nearest stops (BND about $71.6 against $70.0, IEF about $91.8 against $89.5), both small and rate-exposed. MSM closed +5.3% on the day and is now just above its fill.
lessons: L1 follow-up for VNQ: the stored invalidation reads 'about $90.5 if it fills near the 95.73 reference close; re-anchor to the real fill'. It filled at 96.81, so a 5% stop is about $92.0, and $90.5 sits about 6.5% under the fill. Write the re-anchored level into thesis_updates at the next decision instead of leaving a conditional in stored text. The same conditional-wording problem applies to MSM ('roughly $108 only if it fills near the menu close'); that one filled at the menu close, so the level holds.

L5: my pre-open stop distances (IDXX about 676, DPZ about 336) were reasonable but the close was well above them on a +2.4% market day (IDXX about 707). When the decision text gives distances on a mark 4-5% lower, it should say the same for upside days when a trim or re-anchor could be due. IDXX is up about 27% on cost with its $630 stop now about 11% under the mark; consider re-anchoring toward the gain at the next review, as I did on 11-04.

L4 and idle cash: cash stayed near 11.5% and the account was about 10 points less invested than the shadow on a strong rebound day. Taking the $12 VNQ size as roughly a swap for the BTC proceeds was defensible, but the risk-off stance made the net deployment zero. If the tape steadies and SPY holds above 727.64 for another session or two, deploy the headroom (about $9 above the buffer) in INCY or a similar non-Technology, non-Staples name rather than keep waiting. This is a note on the cost of caution, not evidence the stance was wrong.
Sequencing worked: sell at 14:25Z, buy at 14:30Z, with the buffer intact. Keep stating sell-first order when a buy depends on sale proceeds to clear the 10% cash buffer.
